To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a hybrid method to build domain-based gene/protein families using InterPro annotations, which can be useful for comparative genomics and annotation of genomes.

we developed GFam, an open source software that provides automatic annotation of gene/family based on the sequence of the gene/protein and its domain architecture, and GFam can be used for genome annotation, functional studies, and comparative genomics.

GFam is an open-source software that provides a framework to build domain-based gene/protein families, derive meaningful labels and offers a framework for genome annotation initiatives and model organism databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel approach to annotate gene/protein families using a combination of domain-based and sequence-based approaches.
the development of GFam, a novel approach for automatic annotation of protein families.
the development of computational methods for the analysis of large-scale data sets and their applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GFam is an integrated approach to build gene families based on domain architecture and is capable of generating higher sequence and residue annotations than any single constituent database within InterPro.
GFam is a powerful tool for annotation of gene families.
GFam is the first software that provides a framework to derive domain-based gene family annotation using the combined annotation from the 12 member databases of InterPro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GFam can be a valuable tool for genome projects to build domain-based gene/protein families and to propagate annotation from existing databases.
GFam can be used for automatic annotation of protein families and can be used by any genome project for annotation of their proteomes.
GFam can be used for automatic annotation of any protein collection and is particularly useful for genome projects that are in the early stages of annotation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GFam can be useful for any genome project or model organism database that is interested in annotating protein families.
GFam provides an effective and efficient way to annotate protein sequences based on the domain architecture and can be used to propagate functional annotation from one genome release to another.
